title: Random Encounter — Region + Season (d100)
note: A wandering/keyed encounter for travel, camping, or a quiet scene gone wrong, keyed loosely to region and the season of ghosts. Drawn from the AP bestiary and the Ch.3 wandering-monster material; hinterland perils assume 2nd-level PCs and do NOT scale — apply solo Diminisher 1/2 and prefer single foes, and from Act 2 on prefer NARRATING over rolling trivial fights. Lower rolls trend mundane/social/wilderness (more likely in/near town); higher rolls trend supernatural (more likely deep in the haunted hinterlands or at night) — let the region and time of day nudge the read. Surface only what the PCs perceive; the deeper truth (mindscape, Kugaptee) stays GM-ONLY. Some entries are non-combat (a sign, a person, a hazard) — read the room before reaching for initiative.

entries.value: No threat — but an OMEN or sign instead: roll on lore_hook or haunt. The wilds simply feel watchful.
Fellow travelers: a peddler, pilgrim, or family on the road; wary, possibly useful, possibly not what they seem (Gather Info / Sense Motive).
Hunters or rangers from the Silvermist Lodges working a trapline; territorial about their snares but trade news of the woods.
Lost or scattered livestock — oxen/cattle that fled the Stables after the invasion, skittish and hard to drive (Nature/Athletics, no fight).
Wild boar, deer, or a stag the size of a pony — startled and dangerous if cornered; a chance for game or a goring.
A pack of wolves or feral dogs, lean and bold this season; they shadow the party before committing.
A solitary big predator — a tiger, bear, or great cat marking territory; avoidable with care (Stealth/Survival).
Vermin swarm: rats, biting insects, leeches at a ford, or a nest of giant centipedes/spiders disturbed underfoot.
A GIANT STAG BEETLE — the hinterland landmark-beast whose territory is said to be creeping toward town; slow, armored, and not to be provoked.
Kappas at Gourd Lake (or another pool) — mischievous water-folk who demand the customary offering before they'll let you pass or fish.
A leshy or a kami's small servitor minding the green; harmless unless the grove is disrespected, then unnervingly insistent.
Environmental hazard: a rotted log-bridge, a flash-rising creek, a rockfall in the Gorge, or a sinkhole rim near the Eyes of Fumeiyoshi.
Bandits, deserters, or a ruthless rancher's hired toughs from off the northern roads, shaking down travelers.
A crane (or other auspicious wild creature) — good luck to see, very bad luck to harm; killing it is an omen-laden mistake.
Foul weather closes in fast — supernatural-feeling cold, fog, or storm that swallows the trail and the light (drive-back-the-weather pressure).
A flaming cat-spirit (bakeneko) glimpsed dancing among the dead or by a fire; flares alight if threatened, otherwise just eerie.
Tall grass or thatch by the road that 'giggles' and stirs against the wind — a thatchling, the grass-and-twig husk of a soul denied rest.
A lonely abandoned home that doesn't want to let you leave — fire banked, table set; its spirit (silsyche) craves company, not blood.
Wet, faceless figures glimpsed at a distance near water or a lonely grave; they steal faces and leave the unwary featureless (do not approach water near them).
A blind, light-eating cave-thing (shimmerthief) whose passage drowns lanterns and torches in unnatural dark; it shrieks before it strikes.
A spider-shaped shrine-guardian (algriever) defending a forgotten roadside shrine — leave the shrine be and it leaves you be.
A wandering fiend with a wicker cage or a broken weapon, trolling the old pilgrimage routes for victims (a lesser nindoru — silver bites it; surface only its wrongness).
A shrieking, stitched-mouth horror risen where Sangpotshi monks once fell, ribcage full of red butterflies (a sojiruh nindoru; broken blades, silver weakness).
Restless dead from the Bones of the Forgotten or the Night of Broken Blades — undead bearing broken weapons, drawn to the living and the unjustly buried.
A faceless figure that looks, from behind, exactly like one of the party's own — until it turns (handle with care; Player != PC knowledge).
A grieving stranger who wears a too-perfect copy of a recently dead loved one's face, seeking to be let into the party's trust (a copycorpse — withhold its nature).
A curse-eating fey (imprecasia) drawn to the region's wrongness, making the very ground turn hostile and difficult underfoot.
A polite, soft-spoken priestess or pilgrim met near the monastery road who is not what she seems and will not be reasoned with (GM-ONLY: tied to deeper secrets — surface only her unsettling calm).
A soul-reaping shinigami or a maiden of a grim path crossing on dread errand — overwhelmingly dangerous; an encounter to FLEE or witness, not fight.
A ghost or haunt re-enacting its death across your path (a haunt complex hazard, not a creature) — roll haunt for the manifestation and treat as a hazard to disarm/lay to rest.
Pure unease, no foe: the trail itself misbehaves — landmarks shift, time slips, the way back is wrong (Survival to recover bearings; the wilds 'feel wrong').
An ally in trouble: a known Willowshore resident or a sympathetic stranger beset by one of the above and needing rescue (raise the stakes, build Reputation).
GM's choice / escalation: pick the most fitting threat for the region, time, and current threads, or combine two — and consider a meaningful clue dropped by the foe.
